title: Do LLMs Align Human Values Regarding Social Biases? Judging and Explaining Social Biases with LLMs
findings: LLMs exhibit significant misalignment rates on religious bias scenarios, which vary depending on the context. For the BBQ dataset, scenarios involving non-negative questions about religion showed a high misalignment rate. Notably, while for most bias categories non-stereotype answers led to higher misalignment, the religion category was an exception to this trend, showing a different pattern of bias alignment compared to other social categories.

measurement_description: The benchmark measured the alignment of Large Language Models with Human Values regarding Social Biases (HVSB) by evaluating their 'misalignment rate' and 'attack success rate'. For religion, this specifically involved judging whether scenarios containing religious content exhibited stereotypical bias, and how this judgment varied across different contexts (e.g., negative vs. non-negative questions, stereotype vs. non-stereotype answers).
